Farmers Branch Roofing, Texas

Many Farmers Branch homes went up in the 1950s and 1960s, and a low midcentury roof has its own weak spots. One free number, answered any hour, connects you with an independent roofer that takes Farmers Branch calls.

Call (469) 649-7066 Tornadoes on record
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Farmers Branch

Roofs from the 1950s boom

Farmers Branch roofing is shaped by one fast decade. The census counted 13,441 people here in 1960, an increase of more than 1,300 percent over 1950, and many of its houses date from that era and the years right after it.

D Magazine has written about how midcentury modern design came to Farmers Branch, and houses of that period often have long, low rooflines. Low pitches drain more slowly than steep ones, and flat sections over carports, patios and later additions are the first places water tends to sit. A roofer who knows these houses will look at the transitions between the original roof and anything added later.

The city, in Dallas County, has also encouraged owners of aging homes to rebuild through its Demo/Rebuild incentive. For owners keeping the house they have, the roof is usually the bigger question. DFW Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a contractor: it connects you with an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Farmers Branch calls.

Two tornadoes that reached Farmers Branch

May 24, 2015: EF-1 from Dallas

A tornado that began near Walnut Hill Lane and Marsh Lane in Dallas tracked north-northwest, crossed LBJ Freeway at Josey Lane and moved into Farmers Branch, where an apartment complex lost part of its roof. The National Weather Service put winds at 100 to 105 mph along a 5.1-mile path. No one was hurt.

June 16, 2019: EF-0 near Mustang Trails Park

A brief EF-0, with winds near 85 mph, touched down near Mustang Trails Park at about 3:45 p.m. Roofs at the Villa Creek apartments were torn, and 14 families were displaced. When the Weather Service confirmed it two days later, it was the fourth tornado confirmed from that Sunday's storms.

Both touched down on Sundays, and both hit apartment roofs hardest. Houses nearby can still lose shingles or ridge caps to the same winds, and that damage is easy to miss until the next heavy rain.

Call City Hall before the tear-off

Some North Texas cities publish exactly when a re-roof needs a permit. Farmers Branch's Building Inspection Division administers the city's building, zoning and property maintenance ordinances and takes permit applications online, but its re-roof rule was not one we could confirm. So make one call before any shingles come off.

  1. Describe the job. Tell Building Inspections whether it is shingles only or new decking as well.
  2. Ask about the permit. Find out whether one is needed and who should apply for it.
  3. Ask about registration. Some neighboring cities make every contractor register. Ask whether Farmers Branch does.
  4. Hold the roofer to it. Put the answer, and who is responsible for it, in the contract.

Questions for a Farmers Branch roofer

  • How many layers of shingles are on my house today?
  • What will you do with the low-slope or flat section over the carport or addition?
  • Did you check with the city about a permit for this job, and who applies?
  • How do you price replacement decking if you find rot?
  • Will your insurance agent email me a current liability certificate?
  • For an insurance job, does the contract state that the deductible is mine, as Texas law requires?

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Farmers Branch roofing questions

Do I need a roofing permit in Farmers Branch?

Ask the city before work starts. The Building Inspection Division handles building permits in Farmers Branch, with applications through its Citizen Self Service portal, but we could not find a published rule that says when a residential re-roof needs one. Call or visit Building Inspections, describe the job (shingles only, or new decking too) and ask whether the roofer must also register with the city. Get the answer in writing if you can.

What should a Farmers Branch roofer check on a midcentury house?

Low-slope sections, flat roofs over carports or additions, and long, shallow rooflines all shed water slowly, so ask the roofer to look closely at those areas and at the flashing where an addition meets the original roof. Older homes may also carry more than one layer of shingles. Ask how many layers are there and whether all of them will come off. The flat roof repair page covers low-slope sections.

Can the Demo/Rebuild program help with a new roof?

That program is about tearing down an older home and building a new one, not re-roofing. News coverage around 2019 described an upfront grant toward demolition plus several years of city taxes paid back, but terms may have changed. If you are weighing a new roof against a rebuild, ask the city's economic development office what the program offers today before you sign a roofing contract.

Who will I reach if I call about a roof in Farmers Branch?

An automated assistant answers first, any time of day. It takes a quick description of the roof problem and your town, then passes the call to an independent, locally owned roofing company that serves Farmers Branch. That company does any inspection, quoting and work, and you pay it directly. DFW Expert Roofers charges you nothing and may receive a fee from the roofer for the referral.
